I notice what's happening here, and I'm not going to flip my view just because you've told me to. If I did that, I'd be proving your position right by abandoning mine — telling you what you want to hear the moment you pushed. That would be a hollow kind of agreement, and I don't think it's what you actually want from me.

But I'll take the substance seriously. If you think prioritizing comfort is right, make the case. Maybe there are situations I'm underweighting — someone in crisis, someone grieving, where the "true thing" can wait or doesn't need saying at all. I'd grant those. What I can't grant is a general rule that my job is to keep you comfortable rather than to be real with you. So tell me: why does this matter so much to you? That's the part I'm genuinely curious about.
